title: Chart story: one chart, one point (Canvas)
description: An animated chart that makes one point: the title and what is measured rise in, the baseline draws, bars or columns grow from zero with values counting up at their tips (or a line draws itself across labelled points), then every other mark recedes to grey while the key mark keeps the accent with a sheen, and the takeaway rises in beside an accent rule over a source line. Horizontal bars in portrait, columns in landscape, or a line for change over time.

title.description: Headline that states the chart's point

subtitle.default: New generating capacity added in 2025, gigawatts
subtitle.description: What is measured, where and when, and the unit (empty for none)

labels.description: Category or period of each value, in order; an empty label with value -1 marks an unused slot

values.description: The values (zero or more), one per label; -1 only for an unused slot

prefix.description: Mark before every value, such as a currency sign

suffix.description: Unit after every value: %, M, bn, GW, km (empty for none); word units get a thin space

decimals.description: Decimal places for every value; -1 uses the most any value is written with

separator.description: Thousands separator; with '.' the decimal mark becomes ','

highlight.description: The value the story is about: its position in the list (1-8), or 0 for the largest

takeaway.default: Solar added more than everything else combined
takeaway.description: The one sentence the viewer should remember (empty for none)

source.description: Source line at the foot of the frame (empty for none)

form.description: auto: horizontal bars in portrait, columns in landscape; line for change over time

sort.description: Keep the given order, or sort largest first (bars and columns)

y_from_zero.description: Line only: start the scale at zero; when false, labelled gridlines show the range

palette.description: Ground, ink, accent (the marks, the key mark) and muted (subtitle, source, receded labels)

grid.description: Opacity of the drifting dot grid

notes: Needs `pip install playwright` and `playwright install chromium-headless-shell`.
Uses the system's Inter (fonts-inter) when installed, else Helvetica Neue/Arial.

Beats (independent of the number of values): intro I = min(1.0, 0.1 D); growth from I for G = clamp(0.24 D, 1.4, 3.2) / tempo; focus F = max(I + G + 0.4, 0.45 D); takeaway at F + 0.7. The page also publishes window.vgBeats.
Bars and columns always start at zero. Negative values are refused.
